subject: Acadia Labs — renewal & capacity proposal (usage review + SLA clarifications)
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Tan <alex.tan@acadia.ai>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Acadia Labs — renewal & capacity proposal (usage review + SLA clarifications)

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the time last week. I pulled together a short usage & performance snapshot and a recommended path for the upcoming renewal based on Q4 consumption. Attached is a CSV with token-level spend by service and a short latency delta report I pulled from our monitoring. Summary below — happy to walk through in a quick call.

Q4 highlights (Oct–Dec):
- Total tokens: 1.9B (70% Chat, 25% batch embeddings, 5% misc reranking)
- Average 95th pctl latency: 280ms for chat flows (spike to ~450ms during 11/15 incident window)
- Monthly peak concurrency: ~420 concurrent requests (30s+ KV cache hits reduced throughput)
- Effective unit cost (hosted): $0.45 per 1k tokens (post credits/discounts)

Renewal recommendation (two options):
1) Dedicated reserved pool (12m) — commit to 4 GPUs equivalent (predictable throughput + 15% cost reduction)
   - Best for predictability and addressing the concurrency spikes
   - Suggested term: 12 months, 6 months cadence for performance review
2) Hybrid: 6m commit + burst credits — flexible but higher per-token economics

We can also include a one-time onboarding/ingest credit for migration work (I can propose 10% credit on month one if needed).

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-min sync this week? I can pull Rishi and Monica onto the call to firm up the SLA wording and the quote.

Attachments:
- q4_usage_summary.csv (CSV)
- svcs_latency_report.pdf (PDF)

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
[attachment: q4_usage_summary.csv (CSV, 1.1MB)]
From: Alex Tan <alex.tan@acadia.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acadia.ai
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 10:02:13 -05:00
Subject: Re: Acadia Labs — renewal & capacity proposal (usage review + SLA clarifications)

Hi Kimberly — thanks for the snapshot, that helps. Two quick clarifying questions before we lock a time: 

1) The 95th pctl latency number — is that for our production chat model only? We run a small set of low-latency user flows where 95th pctl > 300ms materially impacts UX. Can you break down the latency by model/route?

2) On the Dedicated pool option — what does "4 GPUs equivalent" map to in terms of sustained RPS we can expect during our peak windows? Also please confirm the expected unit cost per 1M tokens under that plan (we need to compare to our internal budget).

I've attached our internal consumption export (small CSV) that shows per-route token counts for Dec.

We are open to a 12m commitment if the economics and SLA are aligned; procurement wants a clear escalation path and credits for systemic incidents.

Thanks —
Alex
Head of Platform, Acadia Labs
alex.tan@acadia.ai
[attachment: acadia_dec_routes.csv (CSV, 320KB)]
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Tan <alex.tan@acadia.ai>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 08:44:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Acadia Labs — renewal & capacity proposal (usage review + SLA clarifications)

Alex — great questions, answered inline below. I pulled the latency split and projected throughput numbers from our telemetry and included the PDF extract.

1) Latency breakdown (95th pctl) by route/model (Dec average):
- prod-chat (gpt-chat-v1): 270ms
- short-response route (gpt-lite-v1): 120ms
- batch/embeddings: N/A (async flows)
- During the 11/15 incident window the prod-chat 95th pctl spiked to ~450ms; root cause was cache eviction during a heavy prefix churn. The attached svcs_latency_report.pdf has the detailed timeline and mitigations.

2) Dedicated pool sizing: our "4 GPU equivalent" is calibrated to sustain ~550 RPS for short chat requests (average tokens ~120) with headroom for bursts up to ~900 RPS before queuing. Under that configuration we model an effective unit cost of ~$0.32 per 1k tokens (roughly 29% lower than your current hosted rate once amortized across the commit).

SLA/credits: for a 12m dedicated commit we can offer:
- 99.9% uptime SLA on the serving tier
- Service credits tiered by p99 latency and availability windows (details on the quote)
- For systemic incidents similar to 11/15, we propose a remediation credit of 5–15% depending on severity (we can tighten the language in the agreement)

If you want, we can surface a formal quote by EOD Wed with an attached redline-ready MPA. We can include a one-time 10% onboarding credit (first invoice) and a 30-day rollback window for the dedicated mapping stage.

Attachments:
- svcs_latency_report.pdf (PDF, 620KB)

Available slots for a 30-min sync: Wed 1/13 09:00–11:00 PT or Thu 1/14 14:00–16:00 PT. Which works?

Best,
Kimberly
[attachment: svcs_latency_report.pdf (PDF, 620KB)]
From: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 12:30:45 -08:00
Subject: Re: Acadia Labs — renewal & capacity proposal (internal)

Internal note — Kimberly, Monica:

I reviewed the numbers; economics look reasonable. Approve offering the 10% one-time onboarding credit for this renewal to close the deal — helps signal partnership and won't materially change ARR. We should also agree to a maximum of 2 SLA credits (escalation matrix) in the MPA and require a post-incident RCA within 5 business days.

Can we pre-authorize a single week of free migration hours (engineer support) and include it in the quote? That will remove the friction Alex's team has flagged.

Rishi
VP, Customer Success
From: Alex Tan <alex.tan@acadia.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acadia.ai
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 07:15:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Acadia Labs — renewal & capacity proposal (usage review + SLA clarifications)

Kimberly — thanks for the level of detail, that addresses most of our concerns. Wed 1/13 09:00 PT works for a 30-min call; please send a calendar invite.

A couple of asks for the meeting:
- Please include a draft MPA with the SLA language and the proposed credits (we will circulate redlines to procurement during the call).
- Confirm the formal quote number (line item for reserved pool, onboarding credit, and 1 week of migration support).

Procurement note: we will likely push pricing down ~8–12% in negotiations. If you can show the committed delta vs hybrid clearly on the quote, that will speed review.

I'll bring our Head of Ops and one engineer on the call. Looking forward to the meeting.

Best,
Alex
